name: DORIS
label: Janine Records
lede: Frank Dorrey, a Linden, New Jersey kid, built a name making surreal portraits on an iPhone, then put out a 50-song, pitched-up sample diary that Pitchfork ranked No. 16 for 2024.

eras.title: An iPhone and a pile of friends' faces
eras.text: Dorrey starts posting art in 2016 and is known as a visual artist long before anyone hears DORIS. The music begins as SoundCloud experiments and turns into a self-run imprint called Janine Records.

years.big: I only work when I get an urge to.
years.h: Frank Dorrey makes his art on an iPhone 8s, lying down
years.p: Frank Dorrey tells It's Nice That he edits in the PicsArt app, usually with YouTube on.
years.xp:
It's Nice That profiles Dorrey's collage-and-illustration work built from photographs of friends, stretched and recoloured into something closer to a dream. Dorrey names Jean-Michel Basquiat, Dean Blunt and Kerry James Marshall among his influences.

He describes a work habit that later shapes the music too: no schedule, only bursts. The piece he discusses, Grossly Invested, came out of the pressure he felt from people wanting to work with him.

years.src: Bandcamp: DORIS, MOLLYWOOD · SoundCloud: DORIS, Janine Records
years.h: MOLLYWOOD goes up on his own Bandcamp
years.p: Five songs, including "SUMBODY GOIN 2 JAIL" with Sailor Goon.
years.xp:
The tracklist is MOLLYWOOD, LUV ME AS I AM, MOLLY w PPL, BEST OF ME and SUMBODY GOIN 2 JAIL, with Sailor Goon on the last.

Earlier that year DORIS had collected four tracks (BUSS DOWN, cry love, PR0BLEM$ and Faygo, posted between April 27 and May 13, 2021) in a SoundCloud playlist titled Janine Records and tagged "we don't end." That is the first appearance of the name that later sits on the credits of the 2024 album.

eras.title: The art world knocks, the rap world listens
eras.text: Dorrey's pictures start turning up in features and on musicians' radar, while DORIS the rapper shows up on other people's records. He says himself he is stuck in a rut, then gets a verse onto a Niontay project.

years.h: CVLT Nation calls his phone paintings "straight Punk Rock"
years.p: Writer Sean Reveron praises Dorrey for balancing colours and vibes while making everything on a phone.

years.h: Vice says Virgil Abloh once wanted a project with him
years.p: The profile says Dorrey collaborated with designer Kerwin Frost and skater William Strobeck, and that the late Virgil Abloh approached him.
years.xp:
Vice calls him a Brooklyn-based artist of Haitian descent who layers faces from his camera roll, sourced from family and friends, until they feel familiar and strange at once. He describes the effect as "a place where I'm distant but also close."

He also tells Vice he is in a "weird rut" after the pandemic and unsure where the work goes next. His recent pictures, he says, were shaped by YouTube rabbit holes of 80s euro punk and African noise rock.

years.h: DORIS takes a verse on Niontay's Dontay's Inferno
years.p: He appears on "10/4," track 5 of [[Niontay|f82718b9-abf9-4dc1-8c0e-eea218c2b973]]'s 2023 album, a record filed under chipmunk soul and experimental hip-hop.

eras.title: The year both careers meet
eras.text: A Chinatown gallery show, a 50-track release through his own label and a Pitchfork ranking land within months of each other.

years.cap: A Dorrey work on the wall at Freedom Love, WHAAM!, Chinatown, January 2024.
yt: WHAAM! Talk: Frank Dorrey and Brayan Ramales
years.h: Dorrey and Ramales take over a Chinatown mall for Freedom Love
years.p: Airbrushed paintings and digital collages by Dorrey, shown beside Brayan Ramales at WHAAM!, 15 Elizabeth Street, through February 17.
years.xp:
Interview Magazine covers the show as two artists building a world inside a Chinatown mall. Dorrey says making the work is "a form of therapy" that lets him think back and piece memories together, and notes he was studying animation at the time.

Office magazine describes his distorted characters as memories compressed into dreamlike states, in colours "too dark and too bright." A filmed talk between the two artists is on YouTube.

years.cap: Frank Dorrey on a New York street, c. 2024.
years.src: Album of the Year: DORIS, Ultimate Love Songs · Discogs
years.h: Ultimate Love Songs Collection arrives with no label behind it
years.p: Fifty self-produced sampledelic vignettes, from 31 seconds to just over two minutes, released on DORIS's own Janine Records.
years.xp:
Discogs lists it as a self-released digital collection of 50 files, the shortest 31 seconds and the longest just over two minutes, with the phonographic copyright held by Janine Records. Album of the Year files it as a compilation under experimental hip-hop, sampledelia and plunderphonics.

Pitchfork's review, by Samuel Hyland, scored it 8.3, according to Album of the Year's listing. Listeners on that site split: one calls it vignettes that rarely stay on an idea past a minute, while others found the vocals hard going.

years.src: Album of the Year: DORIS, The Saver
years.p: Seven tracks in under seven minutes, filed as hypnagogic pop and sound collage: the shortest thing he has made.

yt: Live in Washington D.C., November 21, 2024 (full set)
years.h: DORIS tells SleepWalker Radio he is unsigned
years.p: In a 56-minute interview he traces his path from Linden to Brooklyn to New York City.
years.xp:
The episode covers his high-school beat-making under his own name, his move into rapping and self-producing (mostly in GarageBand), his indie phase and where the DORIS name came from. He names collaborators including Hernbean 5150 and Niontay, and says he is not signed to anyone.

The show notes also announce an upcoming tour with Body Meat and Anycia Kim. Below the interview, a full DORIS set filmed in Washington D.C. on November 21, 2024.

years.src: Album of the Year: DORIS, Ultimate Love Songs · Wikipedia
years.h: Pitchfork puts it at No. 16 of 2024
years.p: Reviewer Samuel Hyland's line, per Album of the Year, which also lists the No. 16 placement on Pitchfork's 50 Best Albums of 2024.
years.xp:
Hyland goes on to call it "a 50-song catalog of memories, half-thoughts, and moments of discovery." Album of the Year lists Pitchfork's score as 83 out of 100.

A Pitchfork feature earlier in the year had already introduced him as a rapper and visual artist putting a surreal twist on everyday life, per the citation on his Wikipedia page.

years.h: Nice To Finally Meet You opens at Good Mother Gallery in LA
years.p: An installation show that runs to January 4, 2025, his first listed outing with the Los Angeles gallery.

eras.title: More of everything
eras.text: After the ranking, DORIS keeps releasing on his own terms and plays campus rooms and clubs, in New York and in Lausanne. A second, bigger compilation gathers older material.

years.src: Album of the Year: DORIS, Dragon Ball Zoe · Oberlin
yt: Live at Le Romandie, Lausanne, December 6, 2025
years.h: Dragon Ball Zoe adds a five-song EP to the pile
years.p: Its tracks include "all nitez" and "fanz in the lobby."
years.xp:
That spring, on April 25, DORIS played 'Sco (the Dionysus Club) at Oberlin College, where the school billed his music as "moody, snippet-sized journeys" built from pitched-up melodies and self-produced beats drawing on kompa, disco, Southern rap and soul.

Two live sets are below: Coyote Studios on June 22, 2025, and Le Romandie in Lausanne, Switzerland, on December 6.

years.src: Apple Music: Everything Else · Album of the Year: DORIS, Everything Else
yt: Live at Turtle Island, NYC, May 10, 2026
years.p: A second compilation on Janine Records, 1 hour 13 minutes long. Pitchfork's Jude Noel gave it 7.6, per Album of the Year.
years.xp: Apple Music lists it as a 45-song release, copyright 2026 Janine Records. One fan on Album of the Year describes it as DORIS's second compilation and welcomes the unreleased mixtape material on it, while wishing for another project, Katz, to be included.
